column1: # Samples excluded from the reprocessing worklist after alignment QC.
# All 18 come from PRJNA217052 (Brito Fiji) and were the only samples in the
# 466-sample reprocessing run to align below 50% against either catalogue
# (cohort median 88.0% UHGG / 88.9% lev). Verified against ENA sample records
# on 2026-08-17; see workflow/scripts/alignment_qc.py in the preprocessing repo
# for the check that surfaced them.
#   Livestock faecal samples deposited alongside the human ones. ENA reports
#   for these -- identical to the 224 human stool samples in the same project.
#   The only distinguishing field is sample_alias: humans carry subject IDs
#   (HUGE-05-12.ST, M1.1.SA), animals carry village.species.AST, where the
#   species token repeats across the three villages M / NK / NV as C (2 per
#   village), P (up to 3) and H. Median 19.1% alignment and 4 detected SGBs
#   against 89.3% and 103 for the human samples in the same study.
#   SAMN02334228 is human stool (alias HUGE-B-09-08.ST) but retains only
#   323,658 read pairs after QC and host removal -- the minimum across all 466
#   samples -- and detects 0 SGBs above 10% breadth. Excluded on depth, not
#   host. Its pre-fetch base_count passed the 100 Mb screen, so only the
#   PRJEB11419 is the American Gut Project. These three carry ENA country
#   and the candidate sweep labelled them H-G purely from geography -- every
#   one of the 142 American Gut rows already in M1 is Industrial. Adding them
#   as non-industrial would be plainly wrong, and adding three more
#   self-selected citizen-science participants as Industrial adds nothing the
#   cohort does not already have. Excluded on the label, not on the data;
#   reinstating them is a one-line edit if that call is revisited.
# None of these 21 appear in metadata_M1.csv, metadata_Mar_16_2026.csv, or any
# existing coverage matrix (UHGG / lev / combined / chimp), so no published
# result is affected. They entered only through the 2026 candidate sweep.
